# Brisbane’s Octopus Deploy quietly wraps tentacles around $45.6 million investment

Brisbane’s Octopus Deploy has $45.6 million more in funding to grow its operations and help developers ship better code.

Octopuses are quiet but deeply impressive. So too was Insight Partners’ latest investment into Brisbane-born tech company Octopus Deploy, bringing its valuation to $882 million.

That capital injection, worth $45.6 million (US$30 million) at time of writing, comes as the startup turns from bootstrapped profitability to more aggressive expansion.

Founded in 2012 by Paul and Sonia Stovell, Octopus Deploy helps software teams deploy, verify, and stress-test new code at the enterprise scale.

It counts more than 300 employees and boasts more than 4,000 customers, who have used the platform for 426 million code deployments.

The release management tool took on a $2 million investment from [Red Gate Software in 2014,](https://www.smartcompany.com.au/startupsmart/octopus-deploy-gets-set-to-unfurl-its-tentacles-after-2-million-investment-from-red-gate/) but truly made its presence known outside the industry in 2021, when New York City-based Insight Partners firm [invested $223 million](https://www.smartcompany.com.au/startupsmart/octopus-deploy-bootstrapped-profitable-223-million-funding/).

As first reported by the [_Australian Financial Review_](https://www.afr.com/technology/qld-tech-firm-s-revenue-rockets-after-major-us-vc-investment-20251007-p5n0lb) _(AFR)_ on Wednesday, Octopus Deploy has since secured millions in extra funding from its major VC backer.

The latest capital injection reportedly bumped its valuation from around $760 million.

It also assisted Octopus Deploy’s acquisition of US company Codefresh in 2024 to build out its market offering.

Speaking to the [_AFR_](https://www.afr.com/technology/qld-tech-firm-s-revenue-rockets-after-major-us-vc-investment-20251007-p5n0lb), Paul Stovell said the company has turned its long-running focus from out-and-out profitability to increasing its scale and revenue.

That appetite for size is obvious in its Q2 investor report, published in August, which uses [Atlassian](https://www.smartcompany.com.au/artificial-intelligence/atlassian-browser-company-acquisition-arc-dia-analysis/) — another Australian software titan using [acquisitions to build scale](https://www.smartcompany.com.au/startupsmart/atlassian-acquires-us-developer-platform-dx-1-5-billion/) — as an example.

Atlassian has earned its valuation because it ‘owns’ the planning phase of software development, the report said.

But the market for deploying, releasing, and operating that code is still “up for grabs”.

“Our ambition is to be the industry standard for releasing, deploying and operating software,” the report continued.

Octopus Deploy counted $127 million in annual recurring revenue in its Q2 report, and a growing number of customers spending at least US$100,000 a year.

All told, the business has good reason to celebrate [World Octopus Day](https://www.worldanimalprotection.org/our-campaigns/sentience/animal-awareness-days/world-octopus-day/), which takes place today, October 8.
